title: Phased Merge Scheduler with Decaying Tenant Weights
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Small prefill requests and short-decode chats are being scheduled separately which increases per-token overhead and underutilizes kernel batched paths. Current arbiters either aggressively merge phases (causing latency spikes for high-priority tenants) or fragment them (causing throughput loss). Goal: introduce a Phased Merge Scheduler that opportunistically coalesces compatible prefill/decode phases into short-lived merged slots while using a decaying tenant weight to balance fairness and recent latency sensitivity. The scheduler should incorporate kernel selection feedback (which kernel a merged slot would trigger) and attention-profile heuristics (sparsity, head count estimates) to avoid selecting merge candidates that force slow kernels or cause KV-cache thrashing.
proposal_summary: Implement a two-stage decision pipeline: 1) Candidate collection window (10-40ms) aggregates incoming phases but tags them with predicted decode length and attention sparsity; 2) Merge decision applies a decaying tenant weight where recent SLA-sensitive responses increase a tenant's weight which decays over a tunable half-life. The merge policy penalizes mixes that would select a slower kernel or exceed KV working set heuristics. If a merge is accepted, the scheduler reserves a short shared slot and schedules micro-batches with kernel-hint tags to the runtime. The scheduler exposes metrics and a rollout toggle in the console for canary testing.
success_criteria: 1) 8-12% reduction in per-token cost for interactive workloads with median latency impact <= +6ms for P1 tenants in canary region. 2) No more than 1% increase in P99 latency for high-priority tenants under baseline load. 3) Stable decrease in GPU kernel churn metric by 15% during coalesced periods.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoffs: Merging favors throughput which can add headroom latency for sensitive tenants; decaying weights increase complexity and require careful tuning. Risks: incorrect attention predictions may trigger slow kernels leading to latency regressions; KV cache pressure can increase memory churn. Mitigations: conservative default thresholds, kernel-probing simulation offline, and an automatic rollback if P99 crosses safety thresholds.
implementation_notes:
- Add a lightweight attention-profile estimator at ingress that uses token count, prompt indicator heuristics, and model metadata to predict sparsity and head usage.
- Extend scheduler state to maintain per-tenant recent-latency-score and compute decaying weight with configurable half-life (default 60s).
- Merge evaluator must consult kernel-selection table (cost model) to estimate worst-case kernel latency for merged slot.
- Add metrics: merged_slots/sec, kernel_penalty_estimate, tenant_weight_distribution, kv_working_set_bytes, merged_slot_evictions.
- Provide a runtime hint header so kernel selection can apply optimized path without changing existing kernel interface.
experiment_plan: Phase A: Offline sim using week-long production traces with synthetic weight decay knobs to pick thresholds. Phase B: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for non-enterprise tenants in us-west-2 for 2 weeks. Phase C: Gradual ramp with rollback guardrails at P99 + 10% compared to baseline. We will maintain an A/B cohort with identical models and measure per-token cost and tail latency.
